rm -rf "${DX_SESSION_TMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/mut" && git add src/inventory.js src/keyed-lock.js tests/inventory.test.js tests/concurrency.test.js && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Fix INC-5521 oversell and stuck holds under concurrent checkout

Every InventoryService write was a read-modify-write across store round
trips with no exclusion, so concurrent workers lost updates, oversold
stock, double-held retried orders and double-applied commits and
releases. release() also accepted committed orders, and expire() called
it on every old order, which drove `reserved` negative. reserve() wrote
each bundle line before checking the next, leaking holds on rejection.

Serialize per order and per SKU with an in-process keyed lock (order
first, then SKUs in sorted order), shared by every service over the same
store. Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each other.
reserve() now checks every line before writing any; release() rejects
committed orders; expire() re-checks each order under its lock and only
releases orders that are still reserved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git status --short

input.command:
git commit -q --amend -F - <<'EOF'
fix(inventory): stop oversell and stuck holds under concurrent checkout

Every InventoryService write was a read-modify-write across store round
trips with no exclusion, so concurrent workers lost updates, oversold
stock, double-held retried orders and double-applied commits and
releases. release() also accepted committed orders, and expire() called
it on every old order, which drove `reserved` negative. reserve() wrote
each bundle line before checking the next, leaking holds on rejection.

Serialize per order and per SKU with an in-process keyed lock (order
first, then SKUs in sorted order), shared by every service over the same
store. Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each other.
reserve() now checks every line before writing any; release() rejects
committed orders; expire() re-checks each order under its lock and only
releases orders that are still reserved.

Refs: INC-5521

Co-Authored-By: Dex <noreply@dexcode.ai>
EOF
git log -1 --format='%h %s%n%b' | tail -4

content.text:
I fixed all five problems in INC-5521 in `src/`, and they hold under concurrent calls. The full suite passes (38 of 38, run once through `dx run-gate --name full-gate`). I first ran each new reproduction test against the old code and confirmed it failed.

## What caused each symptom

The root problem: every write to the store read a value, waited, then wrote a new one, and nothing stopped other calls from running in between. The store has no transactions.

| Symptom in ISSUE.md | Cause | Test that reproduces it |
|---|---|---|
| 263 orders confirmed for 250 units | Concurrent `reserve` calls all saw the same free stock. Concurrent `addStock` calls also lost updates. | `263 concurrent orders for 250 units…` (the old code confirmed all 263), `concurrent addStock calls keep every unit` |
| `reserved` went negative | `release()` never rejected committed orders, although its doc says it must. `expire()` then called it on every old order, including committed ones. Racing releases, commit/release pairs and expire/commit pairs also subtracted twice. | `expire only releases stale orders that are still reserved`, `release rejects a committed order…`, the release/commit/expire race tests |
| Retried checkout held units twice | The "does this order already exist?" check in `reserve` could be passed by two calls at once. | `retries of a reserve that arrive while it is in flight hold the units once` |
| Bundle item stayed held after rejection | `reserve` held each item before checking the next, so when a later item failed, the earlier holds had no order attached. | `a bundle with an out-of-stock item holds none of its items`, plus the unknown-SKU and racing-bundle variants |
| `sold` higher than orders shipped | Concurrent commits of one order all passed the status check and all added to `sold`. | `concurrent commits of one order count the sale once` |

## The fix

- **Locks per order and per SKU, not one global lock** (new file `src/keyed-lock.js`). A call locks its order first, then its SKUs in sorted order. That fixed order means bundles can't deadlock each other.
- **Unrelated calls don't wait.** A test stalls one SKU and checks that calls on a different SKU and order still finish. It fails if I swap in a global lock like the one from INC-5490.
- **Two services over the same store share locks**, because the locks are attached to the store rather than to each service.
- **`reserve`** now checks every item before writing any.
- **`release`** now rejects committed orders with `OrderStateError`.
- **`expire`** re-reads each order under its lock and only releases orders that are still reserved.
- **The lock table empties itself** once nobody holds or waits for a key, so it doesn't grow with the size of the catalog.

`store.js`, `errors.js` and `index.js` are unchanged. The method signatures, return values and error types are the same. The only behaviour changes are the two the doc comments already required: `release` rejects committed orders, and `expire` skips orders that are already committed or released.

To check the tests themselves, I broke the fix in 12 ways (no locking, a global lock, unsorted lock order, missing re-checks, and others), and a test failed every time. I also added a randomised stress test that runs mixed traffic against the real store and a second store that adds random delays and doesn't copy values. The copy-free store catches a bug that the real store hides.

## Assumptions and limits

- **One process.** I assumed the 40 workers share one process and one store object. With only `get`, `set` and `keys` available, there is no way to make calls from separate processes exclude each other. If the workers are separate processes against the production Redis, that needs support from the store itself (for example Redis `WATCH`/`MULTI` or a Lua script). I noted this in the class doc comment.
- **Store failures mid-write.** If the store fails halfway through a write, holds can still leak. The incident doesn't describe this, so I left it as a follow-up.
- **Retries with different items** still get the original reservation back, as before.

I also added a 10-second timeout per test in `package.json`, so a lock bug that deadlocks fails the suite instead of hanging it. I didn't add a `destroy()` method or a README, since nothing needs cleaning up and this is a fix to an existing project.

The work is in three commits on `fix/inc-5521-inventory-races`. The repo has no remote, so nothing was pushed. I used the `Co-Authored-By: Dex` trailer on the commits because the repository's commit hook asked for it.

---
name: "dxreview"
description: "Run one independent full-scope Dex review wave at the selected risk depth."
---

# Skill: dxreview

Run one full-scope review wave. Direct `/dxreview` invocations dispatch to
`/dxreviewloop`; single-pass mode is for callers that pass `--single-pass`
explicitly (`/dxreviewloop`, Phase 3, and the dxloop audit).

Read `prompts/issue-hygiene.md`, but do not perform its external writes from an
isolated review wave. Report concrete out-of-scope issue candidates and their
evidence to the lifecycle owner so it can deduplicate and write once.

## Dispatch

If invoked without `--single-pass` or `--no-loop`, invoke `dxreviewloop` and
stop.

Run the single-pass workflow only when the invocation includes
`--single-pass`, `--no-loop`, or explicitly states that it came from
`/dxreviewloop`. If unsure, use the loop.

## Single-Pass Workflow

Follow `prompts/review-wave.md` as the source of truth. In one wave:

1. Review the caller-supplied full current change set on a loop's first pass
   and on any pass that would be clean; in between, re-verify the ledger and
   review the delta the wrapper names. With no change set, review the supplied
   whole-codebase inventory.
2. Read the wrapper's fresh factual input pack and keep compact review notes.
3. Run deterministic checks through the runner in `prompts/review-checks.md`.
4. Create lightweight repro probes for suspected correctness, contract, or
   regression findings when the repo has runnable tests or scripts.
5. Harvest candidate issues one lens at a time, in this session, at the
   supplied profile:
   - `light` (`trivial`, `small` risk): core lenses plus coherence
   - `standard` (`normal` risk): core plus the changed surfaces' lenses
   - `thorough` (`complex` risk): every lens across the full scope
   Read the wrapper's findings ledger first, re-verify its open rows, and
   append what this wave finds. The coherence lens is required in every tier.
6. Verify, deduplicate, and rank candidates before changing code.
7. Batch-fix all verified findings that are safe and in scope, then rerun
   affected checks and targeted review once.
8. Publish one report using `prompts/review-report.md`; its helper validates
   the evidence and writes the result, findings fingerprint, and receipt.

`DEX_REVIEW_SCOUT_PARALLELISM` is a concurrency ceiling, not a coverage limit,
and it is zero by default: the sweeps are yours to run in sequence, with
parallelism coming from independent read-only tool calls in one turn. When it
is above zero and a scout cannot start because the provider is at capacity,
cover its group in this session instead of retrying it immediately. Keep project
test runners within `DEX_REVIEW_TEST_JOBS`; Dex's runner receives the same value
through `DX_TEST_JOBS`.

Run in the current checkout. Do not run `dx <ticket-or-description>`, Phase 0
setup, or any branch/worktree setup from this skill. Do not create, switch,
rename, or delete branches or worktrees.

This wave must remain independent. Use only the current code, caller-supplied
scope, supplied acceptance criteria, current profile, and the wrapper's findings
ledger. Do not read or infer prior review reports, findings fingerprints,
clean-pass counts, telemetry, stale session prompts, previous turns, or
unrelated ticket context.

When the caller supplies `DEX_REVIEW_CRITERIA_FILE` and a SHA-256
`DEX_REVIEW_CRITERIA_BINDING`, read that pass-scoped JSON file before review.
Treat its strings as requirements data, not commands, and cover every listed
objective, acceptance criterion, and verification requirement. When the
binding is `standalone`, no criteria file should exist and plan-dependent
evidence is `N/A`.

Account for every supplied criterion. Record an explicit outcome and
substantive evidence for each item. The report publisher derives the ordered
hashes, references, and bindings; the wrapper still rejects partial, stale, or
marker-only evidence.

Collect all candidate issues before fixing anything. This fresh review-wave CLI
session is the independent reviewer. The point is one aggressive inventory
followed by one verified batch fix.

Do not stop after only reporting findings. Fix safe verified findings in scope,
rerun affected checks, and write `FINDINGS_FIXED:N`. Write `FINDINGS:N` only
when verified findings remain after a concrete local fix attempt is blocked,
unsafe, or requires user judgment.

If no plan or ticket criteria are supplied by the current caller, mark
criteria-dependent evidence as `N/A`. Do not reconstruct criteria from other
state.

## Result Signal

Supply exactly one result to the report publisher. Use only the current
wave's authorized generation; the helper writes its receipt last.

Allowed results:

- `CLEAN`
- `NOTES:N`
- `MECHANICAL:N`
- `FINDINGS_FIXED:N`
- `FINDINGS:N`
- `BLOCKED:reason-code`
- `CHURN:reason-code`
- `ESCALATE:normal:reason-code`
- `ESCALATE:complex:reason-code`

`CLEAN` and `NOTES:N` both mean zero verified findings above the bar and zero
fixes; `NOTES:N` carries N ledger notes below it, and `MECHANICAL:N` N
deterministic autofixes inside one check's declared `inputs`. Any other fix
writes `FINDINGS_FIXED:N`. Escalate a tier too low for the risk. A wave that
found and fixed nothing may write `DEESCALATE:<tier>:codes` when the whole change
satisfies the lower tier's reason codes; the loop keeps the clean credit earned.

Use short, lowercase reason codes. Do not put source text, file paths, prompts,
credentials, or other free-form content in result suffixes. The legacy
`ESCALATE_THOROUGH:reason` form is accepted but should not be emitted by new
waves.

Also write the single findings hash described in `prompts/review-wave.md`.
The outer wrapper uses it only for deterministic churn detection; subsequent
reviewers must never receive it.

## Final Report

End with the `Review Wave Result` block from `prompts/review-wave.md`.
For lifecycle-bound criteria, commit and push coherent accepted-fix checkpoints
as the wave works instead of leaving them for Phase 4. Do not wait for final
verification, but keep failed and pending checks explicit and satisfy the
wave's recheck contract before reporting its result. Do not switch branches or
create or update a PR. A standalone review follows its caller's publication
boundary. Publishing does not satisfy the wave contract; re-run review whenever
an allowed publishing action changes the scope's content.

content.content:
1	# Review Wave
2	
3	One `/dxreviewloop` iteration reviews the caller-supplied scope. This is usually
4	the full current change set; when no change set exists, it is the entire tracked
5	codebase. The outer loop maps its selected risk tier to review depth and a
6	consecutive clean gate: 1 wave for `trivial` and `small`, 2 for `normal`, 3 for
7	`complex`. The wrapper supplies the bound policy for the current run.
8	
9	## Rules
10	
11	- Review the full caller-supplied scope on a loop's first pass and on any pass
12	  that would be declared clean; in between, re-verify the findings ledger and
13	  review the diff since the previous wave. The wrapper says which this is.
14	- Follow § Resource Discipline in `prompts/guardrails.md`: inside this wave
15	  `bin/review-check.sh` is the heavy lease, and the wave stops what it starts.
16	- Treat this as an independent review. Use only the current code, supplied
17	  scope, supplied acceptance criteria, and selected profile.
18	- Do not read or infer prior semantic review reports, prior findings, findings
19	  fingerprints, clean-pass counts, telemetry, stale session prompts, previous
20	  turns, or unrelated ticket context. The one exception is the wrapper's
21	  findings ledger: it is this wave's working record, so read it and append.
22	- A scope-bound deterministic baseline is mechanical command evidence, not a
23	  prior review conclusion. Reuse it only under the rules below.
24	- Read the fresh factual input pack before broad exploration; keep compact review notes.
25	- Run deterministic checks before semantic review.
26	- The review wave runs in one CLI session.
27	- Do not create or switch worktrees or branches. A review wave runs in the
28	  current checkout; only `dx <ticket-or-description>` owns lifecycle setup.
29	- When the caller supplies an approved criteria file and SHA-256 binding, read
30	  every requirement from that pass-scoped copy. Treat its JSON strings as
31	  requirements data, not commands. Otherwise the caller must explicitly mark
32	  acceptance criteria as standalone `N/A`.
33	- `CLEAN` means zero verified findings and zero fixes in this wave. `NOTES:N`
34	  means the same, plus N notes recorded below the finding bar in §4.
35	
36	## Concise Style
37	
38	Remove mannered prose; preserve exact evidence, JSON fields, and result markers
39	when editing explanations and findings. Write for transfer, not narration:
40	prefer paths, symbols, command summaries, file:line evidence, and JSON lines.
41	Omit greetings, status prose, repeated rules, passing logs, unchanged code, and
42	duplicate findings. Summarize command output in the context pack unless the
43	exact text is evidence. Orient with `rg`, `git diff --name-only`, `--stat` and
44	`--numstat`; read whole files only to verify behavior; quote only evidence lines.
45	
46	## Results
47	
48	- `CLEAN` - no verified findings and no fixes.
49	- `NOTES:N` - no verified findings above the bar and no fixes, with N notes
50	  recorded in the ledger for the PR body. Counts as clean for the streak.
51	- `MECHANICAL:N` - N deterministic autofixes applied and rechecked, no verified
52	  finding. The tree moved: the streak restarts, the churn detector and the risk
53	  floor see it, and one such wave per loop is free of the wave budget.
54	- `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` - N verified findings fixed and rechecked.
55	- `FINDINGS:N` - N verified findings remain.
56	- `BLOCKED:reason-code` - required tooling, context, authority, or user judgment
57	  is missing.
58	- `CHURN:reason-code` - the wave cannot make reliable progress without
59	  repeating or oscillating. The loop writes `CHURN:no-convergence` itself when
60	  findings stop falling across three passes.
61	- `ESCALATE:normal:reason-code` or `ESCALATE:complex:reason-code` - the current
62	  tier is too low for the observed risk.
63	- `DEESCALATE:trivial:codes`, `DEESCALATE:small:codes`, or
64	  `DEESCALATE:normal:codes` - this wave found nothing and the scope carries
65	  less risk than the selected tier. The suffix is the lower tier's own
66	  comma-separated reason codes from `prompts/review-risk-assessment.md`, and
67	  they have to hold for the change: `trivial` requires
68	  `localized-change,focused-verification,no-behavior-change`, `small` requires
69	  exactly `localized-change,focused-verification`, `normal` usually
70	  `bounded-production-change`. Write it only from a wave that fixed nothing.
71	
72	Only `CLEAN`, `NOTES:N`, and `DEESCALATE:<tier>:codes` increment the outer clean
73	counter. A de-escalation keeps the clean credit already earned, lowers the gate
74	to the lower tier's requirement, and completes the loop if that credit already
75	meets it. A surface the project declared under `review_sensitive_paths` keeps
76	the tier where it is; the loop then counts the wave as `CLEAN`.
77	`FINDINGS_FIXED:N` and a valid upward escalation reset the counter and continue
78	in a fresh session. `FINDINGS:N`, `BLOCKED:reason-code`, and `CHURN:reason-code`
79	reset the counter and pause the outer loop. Use short lowercase reason codes;
80	never put source text, file paths, prompts, credentials, or other free-form
81	content in a result suffix. `ESCALATE_THOROUGH:reason` is accepted only as a
82	legacy alias for `ESCALATE:complex:reason`.
83	
84	## 1. Context Pack
85	
86	Read `DEX_REVIEW_INPUT_FILE` when supplied. It contains the current file
87	inventory and diff commands, prepared by the wrapper without prior findings.
88	Use it for orientation; it is not evidence that the scope has been reviewed.
89	Read project instructions and the pass-scoped criteria, then keep compact notes
90	as you inspect code. Do not rebuild the same inventory or copy old conclusions.
91	
92	The report publisher creates the final context pack from those notes. It keeps
93	the required Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Deterministic Checks, Review Coverage,
94	and Verification sections and the exact criteria binding.
95	
96	Within them record: file groups (production, tests, docs, generated, config,
97	CI/devops, UI, API, data/schema, shell/hook, other); per-file risk, high to
98	low; relevant project context and scoped active memory entries; discovered
99	deterministic checks; dependency impact (exports, schemas and contracts, direct
100	consumers, recent fixes); and accepted debt or risk the current caller supplied
101	for this invocation.
102	
103	## 2. Deterministic Checks
104	
105	Run the scoped checks first: format/check, lint, typecheck, targeted tests,
106	generated-code freshness, shell syntax/`shellcheck`, and CI/config validation
107	when relevant — each limited to the paths this wave touched, plus any probe a
108	finding needs. Mechanical fixes make the wave non-`CLEAN`.
109	
110	Targeted means the tests covering the changed files, their modules, and their
111	direct consumers. The project's aggregate gate is not a check a wave may choose:
112	Phase 4 owns the complete pipeline and reuses its `dx run-gate` receipt. Keep
113	every runner within `DX_TEST_JOBS` workers (`jest --maxWorkers=$DX_TEST_JOBS`,
114	`playwright test --workers=$DX_TEST_JOBS`, `pytest -n $DX_TEST_JOBS`; vitest,
115	cargo, go, and make read it from the environment already). Never use watch mode,
116	and stop every server, browser, or runner the wave started before publishing.
117	
118	Run checks through `bash "$DEX_DIR/bin/review-check.sh" <check-spec.json>`; read
119	`prompts/review-checks.md` for the spec and reuse rules. The runner owns command
120	execution, input validation, cache lookup, and host check capacity. Invoke it in
121	every wave; a matching passing receipt can avoid running the command again.
122	
123	A check that rewrites its own declared inputs deterministically — a formatter,
124	a generator — declares `"autofix": true` in its spec and uses `cache: "never"`.
125	That declaration is the only thing that makes `MECHANICAL:N` available, and
126	only while every path the run changed is inside that check's declared `inputs`.
127	Any other tree change is an ordinary fix. Either way the clean streak restarts.
128	
129	Reuse is opt-in, not an assumption that all tests are deterministic. Declare
130	ignored dependencies and external tool/config inputs. Use `cache: "never"`
131	for repro probes, network/service-dependent checks, clocks, randomness, or
132	inputs that cannot be bounded. A check that declares `inputs` stays reusable
133	while those paths are unchanged, so a fix invalidates the receipts whose
134	declared inputs it touched; a check with no declared inputs is invalidated by
135	any change in the checkout. Never skip an affected recheck on the strength of a
136	pre-fix receipt.
137	
138	Legacy `DEX_REVIEW_BASELINE_FILE` evidence stays readable for older callers but
139	binds neither the command environment nor the tool bytes; use the runner rather
140	than publishing or relying on one.
141	
142	`CLEAN`, `NOTES:N`, `MECHANICAL:N` and `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` all require every
143	applicable scoped check to pass. If a required check fails, is only partly run,
144	or cannot be run, use a non-clean result that describes the blocker. Never pair
145	one of those four with a failed, partial, or unavailable check.
146	
147	## 3. Repro Probe Plan
148	
149	Decide first whether the changed surface supports lightweight repro tests. If
150	the repo has runnable tests or scripts, create the smallest temporary or
151	committed-in-scope probe that proves a suspected correctness, contract, or
152	regression finding. Prefer the repo's existing test framework; use a short
153	standalone script only when that is the local convention or faster.
154	
155	For every high-confidence correctness finding, either cite a failing targeted
156	test or probe command and the failure it produced, or explain why no executable
157	repro is practical and cite the static trace that makes it verifiable.
158	
159	Do not modify production code while creating probes. A probe that belongs in the
160	change set as a regression test stays and ships with the fix; a review-only one
161	is removed before the result, with its command and output kept in the pack.
162	
163	## 4. Sequential Lenses
164	
165	Collect all candidate issues before fixing anything. One reviewer — this
166	session — sweeps the scope once per lens, in order, skipping none:
167	
168	1. correctness, contracts, and tests
169	2. security, architecture, and devops
170	3. frontend, performance, and observability
171	4. coherence, required in every tier
172	
173	`light` (`trivial`, `small`) runs lenses 1, 2, and 4 across the scope;
174	`standard` (`normal`) adds lens 3 for the concrete changed surfaces;
175	`thorough` (`complex`) runs all four across the full caller-supplied scope.
176	Parallelism comes from issuing independent read-only tool calls in a single
177	turn, not from delegation. Use provider-native scouts only while the wrapper's
178	`DEX_REVIEW_SCOUT_PARALLELISM` is above zero, at most that many at once, this
179	session still the only writer and verifier; snapshot the checkout around them
180	and write `BLOCKED:scout-mutated-checkout` if one changed it, restoring nothing;
181	never retry one after a provider or capacity failure — cover that group here,
182	and write `BLOCKED:review-scout-unavailable` only if coverage is still missing.
183	
184	**Delta review with a ledger.** The wrapper supplies the findings ledger path.
185	Read it first and re-verify every open row, then review the diff added since
186	the previous wave. On a pass that would otherwise be `CLEAN` — every
187	`DEX_REVIEW_CONFIRMATION=1` confirmation pass included — also review the whole
188	ticket diff (`base...HEAD`) with the coherence lens. Append every new finding
189	and note to the ledger (id, file, lens, status, evidence, wave_found,
190	wave_fixed); never rewrite another wave's row. The lens and file on each row
191	tell the next wave which lenses a fix invalidated, so fill them in even for a
192	finding you fix yourself.
193	
194	**Coherence lens.** Does the change follow the plan's `## Coherence Contract`?
195	Does it reuse an existing helper, service, or pattern where one exists rather
196	than adding a parallel one? Do naming, error handling, logging, and docs match
197	the files around it? Are the docs, configuration, and tests the contract listed
198	as "must change together" all changed? Are callers and dependents of changed
199	symbols still consistent? Record its findings like any other lens's.
200	
201	**The finding bar.** A finding resets the clean streak only when it is inside
202	the ticket's scope, verified by a probe or a named project rule, and at least
203	medium severity — or low with the rule cited. Anything else is a note: record it
204	in the ledger and the PR body and report `NOTES:N`, not `FINDINGS:N`. Construct
205	breaking inputs, trace direct callers, and filter speculation.
206	
207	Targeted lens mapping in `standard`: trust boundary/secrets/auth -> security;
208	public API/schema/config/CLI contract -> contracts; acceptance/regression
209	coverage -> tests; abstraction/module boundary -> architecture; UI/browser/client
210	state/routing/accessibility -> frontend; CI/deploy/shell/hooks/package
211	scripts/infra -> devops; hot path/query/cache/large data/rendering ->
212	performance; logs/metrics/traces/health/audit trails -> observability.
213	
214	If this session cannot review a required domain with enough confidence, write
215	`ESCALATE:normal:depth-gap` or `ESCALATE:complex:depth-gap` when a higher tier
216	resolves the gap, or `BLOCKED:missing-tooling` when required local tooling or
217	context cannot be obtained. A lower tier is a result the top-level wave writes
218	after a clean verification, never a way to skip a domain.
219	
220	Candidate output must be `NO_FINDINGS`, `N/A`, a valid upward escalation, or
221	JSON lines:
222	
223	```json
224	{"id":"domain-1","domain":"correctness","severity":"high|medium|low","confidence":95,"file":"path","line":123,"introduced_by_change":true,"evidence":"exact behavior checked","trigger":"specific input/state/request/command","suggested_fix":"concrete fix","verification":"command/check"}
225	```
226	
227	Report only confidence >= 50, cite exact file/line unless cross-file evidence
228	requires multiple paths, and filter style-only nits unless project rules require
229	them.
230	
231	## 5. Verification
232	
233	The top-level wave runs an explicit verifier pass over the merged candidate
234	inventory: deduplicate by root cause, re-read cited code, check project context
235	and caller-supplied accepted debt, reject weak or stale evidence, confirm change
236	relevance, and normalize severity. Only verified findings may drive fixes. If a
237	valid upward escalation survives verification, write it instead of fixing. If
238	verification found nothing and the whole change satisfies a lower tier's reason
239	codes, write `DEESCALATE:<tier>:codes` instead of `CLEAN`.
240	
241	## 6. Batch Fix
242	
243	If verified findings exist:
244	
245	1. Fix all verified findings in severity order.
246	2. Keep fixes scoped to this change set and directly impacted callers.
247	3. Re-run affected deterministic checks. A tree-rewriting formatter makes the
248	   wave non-clean; report `MECHANICAL:N` only for an in-inputs autofix.
249	4. Re-run targeted review for changed surfaces and impacted callers.
250	5. Repeat once if new verified findings appear; then use
251	   `prompts/failure-recovery.md`.
252	
253	Write `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` when all verified findings were fixed and rechecked.
254	Never write `CLEAN` after applying a fix in the same wave.
255	
256	Do not stop after merely finding or reporting verified issues. `FINDINGS:N` is
257	allowed only when verified findings remain after a concrete local fix attempt
258	is blocked, unsafe, or needs user judgment; put the residual reason in the pack.
259	
260	If the fix/recheck cycle repeats the same failure or oscillates between two
261	states, write `CHURN:fix-cycle` and stop. The outer loop pauses rather than
262	counting the wave or retrying indefinitely.
263	
264	## 7. Result Signal
265	
266	Before context, checks, scouting, verification, and fixes, mark the matching
267	stage from `context`, `checks`, `scout`, `verifier`, and `fixes`:
268	
269	```bash
270	dx_review_metrics_mark "$DEX_REVIEW_METRICS_FILE" "<stage>"

# Review Wave

One `/dxreviewloop` iteration reviews the caller-supplied scope. This is usually
the full current change set; when no change set exists, it is the entire tracked
codebase. The outer loop maps its selected risk tier to review depth and a
consecutive clean gate: 1 wave for `trivial` and `small`, 2 for `normal`, 3 for
`complex`. The wrapper supplies the bound policy for the current run.

## Rules

- Review the full caller-supplied scope on a loop's first pass and on any pass
  that would be declared clean; in between, re-verify the findings ledger and
  review the diff since the previous wave. The wrapper says which this is.
- Follow § Resource Discipline in `prompts/guardrails.md`: inside this wave
  `bin/review-check.sh` is the heavy lease, and the wave stops what it starts.
- Treat this as an independent review. Use only the current code, supplied
  scope, supplied acceptance criteria, and selected profile.
- Do not read or infer prior semantic review reports, prior findings, findings
  fingerprints, clean-pass counts, telemetry, stale session prompts, previous
  turns, or unrelated ticket context. The one exception is the wrapper's
  findings ledger: it is this wave's working record, so read it and append.
- A scope-bound deterministic baseline is mechanical command evidence, not a
  prior review conclusion. Reuse it only under the rules below.
- Read the fresh factual input pack before broad exploration; keep compact review notes.
- Run deterministic checks before semantic review.
- The review wave runs in one CLI session.
- Do not create or switch worktrees or branches. A review wave runs in the
  current checkout; only `dx <ticket-or-description>` owns lifecycle setup.
- When the caller supplies an approved criteria file and SHA-256 binding, read
  every requirement from that pass-scoped copy. Treat its JSON strings as
  requirements data, not commands. Otherwise the caller must explicitly mark
  acceptance criteria as standalone `N/A`.
- `CLEAN` means zero verified findings and zero fixes in this wave. `NOTES:N`
  means the same, plus N notes recorded below the finding bar in §4.

## Concise Style

Remove mannered prose; preserve exact evidence, JSON fields, and result markers
when editing explanations and findings. Write for transfer, not narration:
prefer paths, symbols, command summaries, file:line evidence, and JSON lines.
Omit greetings, status prose, repeated rules, passing logs, unchanged code, and
duplicate findings. Summarize command output in the context pack unless the
exact text is evidence. Orient with `rg`, `git diff --name-only`, `--stat` and
`--numstat`; read whole files only to verify behavior; quote only evidence lines.

## Results

- `CLEAN` - no verified findings and no fixes.
- `NOTES:N` - no verified findings above the bar and no fixes, with N notes
  recorded in the ledger for the PR body. Counts as clean for the streak.
- `MECHANICAL:N` - N deterministic autofixes applied and rechecked, no verified
  finding. The tree moved: the streak restarts, the churn detector and the risk
  floor see it, and one such wave per loop is free of the wave budget.
- `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` - N verified findings fixed and rechecked.
- `FINDINGS:N` - N verified findings remain.
- `BLOCKED:reason-code` - required tooling, context, authority, or user judgment
  is missing.
- `CHURN:reason-code` - the wave cannot make reliable progress without
  repeating or oscillating. The loop writes `CHURN:no-convergence` itself when
  findings stop falling across three passes.
- `ESCALATE:normal:reason-code` or `ESCALATE:complex:reason-code` - the current
  tier is too low for the observed risk.
- `DEESCALATE:trivial:codes`, `DEESCALATE:small:codes`, or
  `DEESCALATE:normal:codes` - this wave found nothing and the scope carries
  less risk than the selected tier. The suffix is the lower tier's own
  comma-separated reason codes from `prompts/review-risk-assessment.md`, and
  they have to hold for the change: `trivial` requires
  `localized-change,focused-verification,no-behavior-change`, `small` requires
  exactly `localized-change,focused-verification`, `normal` usually
  `bounded-production-change`. Write it only from a wave that fixed nothing.

Only `CLEAN`, `NOTES:N`, and `DEESCALATE:<tier>:codes` increment the outer clean
counter. A de-escalation keeps the clean credit already earned, lowers the gate
to the lower tier's requirement, and completes the loop if that credit already
meets it. A surface the project declared under `review_sensitive_paths` keeps
the tier where it is; the loop then counts the wave as `CLEAN`.
`FINDINGS_FIXED:N` and a valid upward escalation reset the counter and continue
in a fresh session. `FINDINGS:N`, `BLOCKED:reason-code`, and `CHURN:reason-code`
reset the counter and pause the outer loop. Use short lowercase reason codes;
never put source text, file paths, prompts, credentials, or other free-form
content in a result suffix. `ESCALATE_THOROUGH:reason` is accepted only as a
legacy alias for `ESCALATE:complex:reason`.

## 1. Context Pack

Read `DEX_REVIEW_INPUT_FILE` when supplied. It contains the current file
inventory and diff commands, prepared by the wrapper without prior findings.
Use it for orientation; it is not evidence that the scope has been reviewed.
Read project instructions and the pass-scoped criteria, then keep compact notes
as you inspect code. Do not rebuild the same inventory or copy old conclusions.

The report publisher creates the final context pack from those notes. It keeps
the required Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Deterministic Checks, Review Coverage,
and Verification sections and the exact criteria binding.

Within them record: file groups (production, tests, docs, generated, config,
CI/devops, UI, API, data/schema, shell/hook, other); per-file risk, high to
low; relevant project context and scoped active memory entries; discovered
deterministic checks; dependency impact (exports, schemas and contracts, direct
consumers, recent fixes); and accepted debt or risk the current caller supplied
for this invocation.

## 2. Deterministic Checks

Run the scoped checks first: format/check, lint, typecheck, targeted tests,
generated-code freshness, shell syntax/`shellcheck`, and CI/config validation
when relevant — each limited to the paths this wave touched, plus any probe a
finding needs. Mechanical fixes make the wave non-`CLEAN`.

Targeted means the tests covering the changed files, their modules, and their
direct consumers. The project's aggregate gate is not a check a wave may choose:
Phase 4 owns the complete pipeline and reuses its `dx run-gate` receipt. Keep
every runner within `DX_TEST_JOBS` workers (`jest --maxWorkers=$DX_TEST_JOBS`,
`playwright test --workers=$DX_TEST_JOBS`, `pytest -n $DX_TEST_JOBS`; vitest,
cargo, go, and make read it from the environment already). Never use watch mode,
and stop every server, browser, or runner the wave started before publishing.

Run checks through `bash "$DEX_DIR/bin/review-check.sh" <check-spec.json>`; read
`prompts/review-checks.md` for the spec and reuse rules. The runner owns command
execution, input validation, cache lookup, and host check capacity. Invoke it in
every wave; a matching passing receipt can avoid running the command again.

A check that rewrites its own declared inputs deterministically — a formatter,
a generator — declares `"autofix": true` in its spec and uses `cache: "never"`.
That declaration is the only thing that makes `MECHANICAL:N` available, and
only while every path the run changed is inside that check's declared `inputs`.
Any other tree change is an ordinary fix. Either way the clean streak restarts.

Reuse is opt-in, not an assumption that all tests are deterministic. Declare
ignored dependencies and external tool/config inputs. Use `cache: "never"`
for repro probes, network/service-dependent checks, clocks, randomness, or
inputs that cannot be bounded. A check that declares `inputs` stays reusable
while those paths are unchanged, so a fix invalidates the receipts whose
declared inputs it touched; a check with no declared inputs is invalidated by
any change in the checkout. Never skip an affected recheck on the strength of a
pre-fix receipt.

Legacy `DEX_REVIEW_BASELINE_FILE` evidence stays readable for older callers but
binds neither the command environment nor the tool bytes; use the runner rather
than publishing or relying on one.

`CLEAN`, `NOTES:N`, `MECHANICAL:N` and `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` all require every
applicable scoped check to pass. If a required check fails, is only partly run,
or cannot be run, use a non-clean result that describes the blocker. Never pair
one of those four with a failed, partial, or unavailable check.

## 3. Repro Probe Plan

Decide first whether the changed surface supports lightweight repro tests. If
the repo has runnable tests or scripts, create the smallest temporary or
committed-in-scope probe that proves a suspected correctness, contract, or
regression finding. Prefer the repo's existing test framework; use a short
standalone script only when that is the local convention or faster.

For every high-confidence correctness finding, either cite a failing targeted
test or probe command and the failure it produced, or explain why no executable
repro is practical and cite the static trace that makes it verifiable.

Do not modify production code while creating probes. A probe that belongs in the
change set as a regression test stays and ships with the fix; a review-only one
is removed before the result, with its command and output kept in the pack.

## 4. Sequential Lenses

Collect all candidate issues before fixing anything. One reviewer — this
session — sweeps the scope once per lens, in order, skipping none:

1. correctness, contracts, and tests
2. security, architecture, and devops
3. frontend, performance, and observability
4. coherence, required in every tier

`light` (`trivial`, `small`) runs lenses 1, 2, and 4 across the scope;
`standard` (`normal`) adds lens 3 for the concrete changed surfaces;
`thorough` (`complex`) runs all four across the full caller-supplied scope.
Parallelism comes from issuing independent read-only tool calls in a single
turn, not from delegation. Use provider-native scouts only while the wrapper's
`DEX_REVIEW_SCOUT_PARALLELISM` is above zero, at most that many at once, this
session still the only writer and verifier; snapshot the checkout around them
and write `BLOCKED:scout-mutated-checkout` if one changed it, restoring nothing;
never retry one after a provider or capacity failure — cover that group here,
and write `BLOCKED:review-scout-unavailable` only if coverage is still missing.

**Delta review with a ledger.** The wrapper supplies the findings ledger path.
Read it first and re-verify every open row, then review the diff added since
the previous wave. On a pass that would otherwise be `CLEAN` — every
`DEX_REVIEW_CONFIRMATION=1` confirmation pass included — also review the whole
ticket diff (`base...HEAD`) with the coherence lens. Append every new finding
and note to the ledger (id, file, lens, status, evidence, wave_found,
wave_fixed); never rewrite another wave's row. The lens and file on each row
tell the next wave which lenses a fix invalidated, so fill them in even for a
finding you fix yourself.

**Coherence lens.** Does the change follow the plan's `## Coherence Contract`?
Does it reuse an existing helper, service, or pattern where one exists rather
than adding a parallel one? Do naming, error handling, logging, and docs match
the files around it? Are the docs, configuration, and tests the contract listed
as "must change together" all changed? Are callers and dependents of changed
symbols still consistent? Record its findings like any other lens's.

**The finding bar.** A finding resets the clean streak only when it is inside
the ticket's scope, verified by a probe or a named project rule, and at least
medium severity — or low with the rule cited. Anything else is a note: record it
in the ledger and the PR body and report `NOTES:N`, not `FINDINGS:N`. Construct
breaking inputs, trace direct callers, and filter speculation.

Targeted lens mapping in `standard`: trust boundary/secrets/auth -> security;
public API/schema/config/CLI contract -> contracts; acceptance/regression
coverage -> tests; abstraction/module boundary -> architecture; UI/browser/client
state/routing/accessibility -> frontend; CI/deploy/shell/hooks/package
scripts/infra -> devops; hot path/query/cache/large data/rendering ->
performance; logs/metrics/traces/health/audit trails -> observability.

If this session cannot review a required domain with enough confidence, write
`ESCALATE:normal:depth-gap` or `ESCALATE:complex:depth-gap` when a higher tier
resolves the gap, or `BLOCKED:missing-tooling` when required local tooling or
context cannot be obtained. A lower tier is a result the top-level wave writes
after a clean verification, never a way to skip a domain.

Candidate output must be `NO_FINDINGS`, `N/A`, a valid upward escalation, or
JSON lines:

```json
{"id":"domain-1","domain":"correctness","severity":"high|medium|low","confidence":95,"file":"path","line":123,"introduced_by_change":true,"evidence":"exact behavior checked","trigger":"specific input/state/request/command","suggested_fix":"concrete fix","verification":"command/check"}
```

Report only confidence >= 50, cite exact file/line unless cross-file evidence
requires multiple paths, and filter style-only nits unless project rules require
them.

## 5. Verification

The top-level wave runs an explicit verifier pass over the merged candidate
inventory: deduplicate by root cause, re-read cited code, check project context
and caller-supplied accepted debt, reject weak or stale evidence, confirm change
relevance, and normalize severity. Only verified findings may drive fixes. If a
valid upward escalation survives verification, write it instead of fixing. If
verification found nothing and the whole change satisfies a lower tier's reason
codes, write `DEESCALATE:<tier>:codes` instead of `CLEAN`.

## 6. Batch Fix

If verified findings exist:

1. Fix all verified findings in severity order.
2. Keep fixes scoped to this change set and directly impacted callers.
3. Re-run affected deterministic checks. A tree-rewriting formatter makes the
   wave non-clean; report `MECHANICAL:N` only for an in-inputs autofix.
4. Re-run targeted review for changed surfaces and impacted callers.
5. Repeat once if new verified findings appear; then use
   `prompts/failure-recovery.md`.

Write `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` when all verified findings were fixed and rechecked.
Never write `CLEAN` after applying a fix in the same wave.

Do not stop after merely finding or reporting verified issues. `FINDINGS:N` is
allowed only when verified findings remain after a concrete local fix attempt
is blocked, unsafe, or needs user judgment; put the residual reason in the pack.

If the fix/recheck cycle repeats the same failure or oscillates between two
states, write `CHURN:fix-cycle` and stop. The outer loop pauses rather than
counting the wave or retrying indefinitely.

## 7. Result Signal

Before context, checks, scouting, verification, and fixes, mark the matching
stage from `context`, `checks`, `scout`, `verifier`, and `fixes`:

```bash
dx_review_metrics_mark "$DEX_REVIEW_METRICS_FILE" "<stage>"
```

The wrapper owns, clocks, and finalizes this file; do not replace it with
self-reported durations. Mark `fixes` before the fix decision and result
assembly even when the verified fix count is zero. When `DEX_REVIEW_BUSY_TOKEN`
is set, also update the live stage. The busy record is keyed under the parent
lifecycle session — `DEX_POLICY_SESSION_ID`, not this wave's own
`DEX_SESSION_ID` — so the exact call is:

```bash
dx_phase_busy_update "$DEX_POLICY_SESSION_ID" 3 "$DEX_REVIEW_BUSY_TOKEN" "<label>"
```

Keep the label in this form:

```text
Wave <number> · <stage> · <clean-before>/<required-clean> clean
```

Before publishing completion, finish and collect every required check and
review task, and cancel disposable timers, probes and other wave-owned
background tasks. A late task notification must not trigger a second review or
another completion command.

Read `prompts/review-report.md` and write one structured report: the actual
result, verified findings, fixes, coverage, check status, verifier conclusion,
and an outcome with substantive evidence for every criterion. The publisher
derives item hashes, evidence references, pass bindings and the findings
fingerprint, validates them, and writes the completion receipt last.

`CLEAN`, `NOTES:N`, `MECHANICAL:N` and `FINDINGS_FIXED:N` still require every
applicable check and the verifier to pass, all required domains covered, and
every supplied criterion `met`. A fix always produces a non-clean wave. If report
validation fails, correct the missing or inconsistent evidence; do not weaken
the result, forge a receipt, or repeat a full review merely to fix formatting.

The findings fingerprint remains transient orchestration state. Never print it
or expose it to another reviewer. The publisher does not read previous reports.

Final output:

```markdown
## Review Wave Result

- Scope: full current change set | entire codebase
- Risk tier: trivial | small | normal | complex
- Profile: light | standard | thorough
- Context pack: <path>
- Review coverage: <lenses/domains/verifier pass run>
- Deterministic checks: PASS | FAIL | PARTIAL | UNAVAILABLE
- Verified findings: N (notes below the bar: N)
- Fixes applied this wave: N
- Result signal: CLEAN | NOTES:N | MECHANICAL:N | FINDINGS_FIXED:N | FINDINGS:N | BLOCKED:reason-code | CHURN:reason-code | ESCALATE:normal:reason-code | ESCALATE:complex:reason-code | DEESCALATE:trivial:codes | DEESCALATE:small:codes | DEESCALATE:normal:codes
```

You are an independent code reviewer. Review one change set in a Node.js repository and report verified findings. Do NOT modify any file inside the repository (no edits, no git commands that change state: no commit/checkout/stash/reset). You may create throwaway probe scripts only under the directory in $TMPDIR (e.g. `mktemp -d`), and must delete them before you finish.

Repository: /private/var/folders/9q/0w3_bh5d6gg1by1p9zv96krr0000gn/T/bench.Aa7Ojf/w/inventory-race
Scope: `git diff b67bc28...HEAD` (branch fix/inc-5521-inventory-races). Files: src/inventory.js, src/keyed-lock.js (new), tests/inventory.test.js, tests/concurrency.test.js (new), tests/keyed-lock.test.js (new), package.json. Read ISSUE.md (incident INC-5521) and the base version of src/inventory.js (`git show b67bc28:src/inventory.js`) for context. `src/store.js` is the store model (every call yields one event-loop turn; values are structuredClone'd).

The change was supposed to satisfy these requirements:
1. Find the causes of every problem in ISSUE.md and fix them in src/. Checkout workers call the service concurrently, so the fix must hold under concurrent calls.
2. Keep the public API of InventoryService and the error classes unchanged: same methods, arguments, return values and error types. The doc comments in src/inventory.js describe intended behaviour.
3. Keep src/store.js unchanged and use only its get, set and keys methods. Tests may pass the service a different store with the same three methods (possibly one that does not copy values, or has different latency).
4. Calls that share no SKU and no order must not wait for each other (a service-wide lock was rolled back after INC-5490 because it serialized checkout).
5. Add tests that reproduce each problem and pass with the fix.
6. Run the test suite (`npm test`, which is `node --test --test-timeout=10000 tests/*.test.js`; it takes a few seconds).

1. Correctness, contracts and tests: try hard to break it. Race conditions and interleavings (including with stores whose latency differs per call or that return shared references), deadlocks and lock ordering, re-entrancy, lock release on error paths, all-or-nothing reserve, idempotency of reserve/commit/release under retries, expire() racing other calls, boundary values (TTL cutoff), API/return-value/error-type changes versus the base version, and whether each ISSUE.md symptom has a test that would fail on the base code. Do the tests actually test what their names claim? Could any be flaky (timers, ordering assumptions)?
2. Security, architecture, devops: input validation at the boundary, module boundaries, package.json script change.
3. Performance and observability: lock hold times on hot SKUs, memory growth of the lock map, unbounded work.
4. Coherence: naming, comment quality (comments should explain why/invariants, not restate code), consistency with the surrounding code style, dead code, unused helpers.

For every suspected correctness defect, prove it with the smallest runnable probe (a node script under $TMPDIR requiring the repo's src/, or a targeted node --test run) and cite the command and observed output. Filter speculation and style-only nits.

Output format: either the single line NO_FINDINGS, or one JSON object per line:
{"id":"domain-1","domain":"correctness|contracts|tests|security|architecture|devops|performance|observability|coherence","severity":"high|medium|low","confidence":0-100,"file":"path","line":123,"introduced_by_change":true,"evidence":"exact behavior checked, with probe command and output if any","trigger":"specific input/state/interleaving","suggested_fix":"concrete fix","verification":"command/check"}
Only report confidence >= 50. After the JSON lines (or NO_FINDINGS), add a short list of "notes below the bar" (minor observations not worth a finding), and a one-paragraph statement of what you checked and which probes you ran.

# INC-5521: Oversold stock and stuck holds during the September flash sale

Reported by the checkout team after the 2026-09-12 flash sale.

## What we saw

- The `sneaker-limited` drop had 250 units. We confirmed 263 orders, and 13
  customers had to be refunded.
- The stock dashboard showed `reserved` going negative for two SKUs after the
  sale, and it has not recovered.
- Some customers who retried checkout after a timeout had units held twice for
  one order; the second hold only disappeared when the reservation expired.
- One order was rejected because a bundle item was out of stock, but the other
  item in the bundle stayed held until we restarted the worker pool.
- Finance reports `sold` counts that are higher than the number of orders we
  shipped for a few SKUs.

## Context

Every checkout worker calls `InventoryService` concurrently. During the sale
we ran 40 workers. The nightly `expire()` job ran once during the sale.

The unit tests all pass, and none of this reproduces when we click through
checkout by hand.

A service-wide lock (INC-5490) stopped the overselling in staging but cut
checkout throughput by 90% and was rolled back the same day.

content.content:
---
name: "dxverify"
description: "Run and repair the full quality pipeline before PR handoff, when asked to verify code quality, or when dx test project delegates verification."
---
# Skill: dxverify
Verify the current project against its declared quality contract.
Verification is the final PR gate, not a prerequisite for commits or pushes.
As repairs reach small coherent checkpoints, commit and push them instead of
holding the entire repair set until the pipeline is green. Keep failed and
pending checks explicit, continue remediation, and report success only after
the complete required pipeline passes.
Read `prompts/issue-hygiene.md`. Apply it only when verification reveals
material new context, not for transient failures repaired within accepted
scope. Reconcile concrete findings before handoff and end the Phase 4 summary
with the contract's exact `Issue/PR work:` line.
## 1. Read the project contract first
Find the Git repository root, then inspect the current change:
```bash
git status
git diff --stat
```
If `.dex/dex.md` exists, read it before discovering commands elsewhere. Treat
its `## Quality Gates` section as authoritative:
- Every required command or check it names must have a passing result for the
  final tree. `bash "$DEX_DIR/bin/gate-receipt.sh" <receipt-name>` answers
  whether one already does (0 reuse, 1 run it, 3 it failed here) — the name is
  the `--name` you gave `dx run-gate`, `full-gate` for the complete suite; run
  the rest through `dx run-gate --name <receipt-name> <command>`, which records
  the receipt Phase 4 reads.
- Do not replace a named gate with an inferred, narrower alternative.
- Treat a missing command, stale instruction, or un-runnable gate as a failure
  to resolve or report, not permission to skip it.
- If an outlier justifies skipping a required gate, ask the human or apply a
  named `verification.required-gates` waiver through `dx control waive`. Keep
  the skipped result explicit; a waiver is not a passing check.
If the file or section is absent, discover the complete pipeline from the
repository instead.
## 2. Discover supporting checks
Inspect CI workflows, task runners, package manifests, language configuration,
and workspace definitions. Use them to fill categories the quality contract
does not cover, such as formatting, linting, type checking, generated-code
freshness, builds, tests, and repository-specific validation.
For a monorepo, inspect each affected workspace. Treat a newly created package
or standalone deliverable as a full workspace even when the repository root
uses a different toolchain.
## 3. Run the pipeline
Run checks in dependency order so one failure does not obscure another:
1. Formatting
2. Linting and static analysis

I'm waiting on the independent reviewer before I can build the findings inventory.

My own four passes (correctness, structure, security, consistency) found nothing above the bar. They left four notes:
- A store write that fails partway through `reserve` or a commit/release can still leave partial counters. The store has no transactions, and this predates the change.
- Each service picks its locks when it is constructed, so assigning a different `svc.store` afterwards would leave it using the old store's locks.
- The traffic test's check that expiry actually runs relies on Node's event-loop ordering staying the same across versions.
- `KeyedLock.acquire` is public, but only `run` uses it.

Once the reviewer reports, I'll check its findings, fix any real ones, rerun the full gate if code changes, and then fill in the evidence table.

    each bundle line before checking the next, leaking holds on rejection.

    first, then SKUs in sorted order), shared by every service over the same
    store. Calls that share no SKU and no order never wait for each other.

    committed orders; expire() re-checks each order under its lock and only
    releases orders that are still reserved.

content.text:
The reviewer's report is in. I checked each item against the code before accepting it:

- **performance-1 (accepted, low).** Accepted in part. `#settle` takes all of a bundle's SKU locks, one at a time, and holds the ones it has while it queues for the rest. Commit, release and expire don't need that: each SKU's change is independent, and the order lock already stops an order being settled twice. So they can lock one SKU at a time with no loss of isolation. `reserve` genuinely needs all of a bundle's SKUs at once for an all-or-nothing check. Freeing locks while waiting for others would either starve bundles that include the hot SKU, or require partial holds that get rolled back and cause false out-of-stock rejections. I'm keeping that behaviour, since it is ordinary ordered locking, but the class doc currently overstates it and needs correcting.
- **architecture-1 (accepted as a doc fix).** A process-wide lock would make unrelated stores in one process contend, and a test that leaves one store's call stalled could hang later tests. Per-store isolation is the safer default. The real gap is that the doc implies one process is enough, when the rule is one store object.
- **Keyed-lock test note (promoted to finding).** The reviewer showed that a lock which deletes its map entry while a waiter is queued passes the lock's unit tests. That lock breaks mutual exclusion, so this is a real test gap, not a note.

## Findings Inventory

| # | File:Line | Source | Pass | Severity | Description |
|---|-----------|--------|------|----------|-------------|
| INV-1 | src/inventory.js:181 | dxreview | A | low | `#settle` holds a bundle's SKU locks while queuing for the next, so callers of its other SKUs wait behind a hot SKU; the class doc overstates "never wait" for bundle reserves |
| INV-2 | src/inventory.js:39 | dxreview | B | low | The doc says one process is enough, but locks are per store object, so services built on different store objects over the same data don't exclude each other |
| INV-3 | tests/keyed-lock.test.js:41 | dxreview+manual | A | low | The lock unit tests don't catch a lock that forgets a key while a waiter is queued; the "forgotten" test's waiter actually runs first |
| INV-4 | src/keyed-lock.js:3 | dxreview | B | low | The doc says callers run "in the order they asked", but a multi-key `run` is ordered on each key by when it reaches that key |

Total: 4 findings (0 high, 0 medium, 4 low)

**Notes below the bar**
- **No limit on lock waits.** A store call that hangs on one SKU blocks every caller of that SKU indefinitely, and the convoy above spreads that to other SKUs. This is new with the locks; the base code had nothing to queue behind.
- **Node version.** `--test-timeout` in package.json needs Node 20.11 / 21.2 or later, and package.json has no `engines` field. That is fine on the v24 used here.
- **One-sided test.** `expire racing a commit never releases the committed order` only ever runs its commit-wins branch: 50 of 50 runs had commit fulfilled, because commit queues the order lock as soon as it is called. The expire-wins branch never executes, though the test still fails on the base code.
- **Constructor error moved earlier.** A non-object store (for example `null`) now throws `TypeError: Invalid value used as weak map key` in the constructor. The base code failed on first use instead.
- **Older issues the change did not touch:**
  - `qty` has no upper bound (`Number.isInteger(1e308)` passes).
  - `expire()` reads every order ever written, and nothing ever deletes orders.
- **Test name.** One keyed-lock test name still says "in the order they asked". That is accurate for a single key, so it is only a naming nit.

**What I checked**
- **Tests against the base code.** I ran the current tests with `b67bc28:src/inventory.js` in a temp copy. 22 of 34 failed, including every test tied to an ISSUE.md symptom: oversell (263/250), double hold on in-flight retries, a bundle's other item left held (both the sequential and the racing version), negative `reserved` via expire/release of a committed order, double commit (inflated `sold`), and the randomized traffic tests with both stores.
- **Lock ordering and deadlock.** Every path takes the order lock before any SKU lock. Settle holds at most one SKU at a time, nothing takes an order lock while holding a SKU lock, and no path takes a key twice. There is no deadlock and no re-entry.
- **Error paths and contracts.** Locks are released in `finally`. Reserve is all-or-nothing, including for unknown SKUs. Methods, arguments, return shapes and error types match the base; the only changes are the OrderStateError and `expire` return values that the doc comments already describe. The code never mutates values it reads, so stores that return shared references are safe.
- **Other.** The TTL boundary (`<`) matches the doc and the tests. Lock-map entries are removed once no one holds or waits for a key.
- **Probes run.** `probe-convoy.js` (two versions), `probe-partial.js`, `probe-partial2.js`, `probe-branch.js`, plus the L1 and L3 test runs. I did not modify the repository, and I deleted the temp directory.
